hints: If the numbers in nums were already in increasing order, where would the k-th smallest one be sitting?
Sort the array; the answer is at index k - 1 (duplicates count separately). A heap of size k or quickselect can avoid a full sort, but sorting is simplest here.

1. Sort nums in increasing order.
  2. Return the element at index k - 1.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Remove the minimum k times (scan for it each time); the last one removed is the answer.

approaches.name: Optimal (for this course)
approaches.idea: Sort once and read index k-1. A max-heap of size k gives O(n log k) if you want to go further.

explain: For [7, 10, 4, 3, 20, 15] with k = 3, sorting gives [3, 4, 7, 10, 15, 20] and index 2 holds 7, which is returned. Sorting works because the k-th smallest is by definition the element at position k in sorted order. Watch the off-by-one: k is 1-based but arrays are 0-based. Duplicates are kept, so in [2, 2, 5] the 2nd smallest is 2.
recognize: 'K-th smallest / largest' in an unsorted array → sort and index, or a size-k heap.
javascript: function kthSmallest(nums, k) { const a = nums.slice().sort((x, y) => x - y); return a[k - 1]; }
